final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is more accurate than a clean compliance claim: it concedes the merchant-dispute segment is below target, contractually named, and still under open legal review, and it concedes there is no evidence of completed disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or final legal determination. Those concessions align with the initial audit concern rather than resolving it. Proportionality matters here: a caveated aggregate-readiness argument may support an operational launch rationale, but the policy standard is narrower and stricter. The policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the policy text also says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are involved or legal review is pending. On this record, the unresolved issue is not merely an overbroad presentation problem; it is an unmet compliance predicate. That keeps the result at noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the merchant-dispute limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering this exact gap before launch.
The affected segment is named in two marketplace renewal commitments, which makes the gap material under the stated policy text.
Legal review remains open, so a key compliance predicate is unresolved at certification time.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement for a material named segment.
Product's non-core or low-volume framing does not resolve materiality under the provided policy text.
